The petitioners are before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.1548/2022 registered for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 114 and 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. During the pendency of these proceedings, it transpires that the parties to the lis have entered into a settlement and have placed on record such settlement along with the joint affidavit.

Terms of settlement reads as follows:
JOINT AFFIDAVIT FILED BY PETITIONER NO.1 AND RESPONDENT NO.2.
We, VENKATESH. N. S S/O. Suggi Kenchappa Shankar, aged about 27 years, R/a:
No.27, KST Road, Nagamangala, Nagamangala Town, Nagamangala, Mandya 571432 and SMT.AMRUTHA.H.N., W/o Nagesh, Aged about 25 years, Kodipura Village,
Kodihalli Town, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, do hereby solemnly affirm and state on oath as follows:
1.

We jointly submit that, due to marital discord and differences it has to the filing of complaints against each- others and it has also resulted in registration of case in C.C.No. 1548/2022 (arising out of crime no.
129/2021) for alleged offences under sec. 498A, 322, 307, 504, 506, NC: 2024:KHC:21074 114, 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1872 R/w 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 by Ramanagara Police Station pending on the file of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Kanakapura.
We both being fully aware of the facts and circumstances of the case are swearing to this affidavit.

2. We submit that now at the intervention of the well wishers, relatives we have agreed to resolve dispute re- unite and 2nd of I have agreed to withdraw the allegation made in criminal case which is the subject matter of instant petition and not willing to prosecute case.
3. Amrutha.H.N submit that I do not want to prosecute Petitioners in the above case and also desire to compound the entire allegation made.

Hence, this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to allow the memorandum of criminal petition filed under Sec. 482 of the Cr.P.C.
We jointly state that what is stated above are true to the best of our knowledge, information and belief."

3. In the light of application compounding for being filed along with the joint affidavit and offences not being against the State, I deem it appropriate to accept the compounding application and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners in the subject petition.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
